My Tools💻
FREE MONTH voice to text: https://get.glaido.com/nate
Code NATEHERK for 10% off VPS (annual plan): https://www.hostinger.com/vps/claude-code-hosting

I gave Claude Code a horrible coffee shop website and told it to make it better 100 times in a row, once with Sonnet 5.5 and once with Opus 5.5.

Sonnet made small, careful changes, while Opus kept adding features until the site hit 21,000 lines and started breaking itself. Neither model searched the web once, even though it could, and in this video I walk through every milestone and what it means for how you prompt AI.

comments.text: Iterative prompting without clear constraints is dangerous. Claude probably started hallucinating after a few iterations.
comments.author: @alemaestree

comments.text: If you force it to add something every time, then it’s gonna add something 100 times, and that’s what’s gonna happen.

comments.text: Lots of good ideas in this coffee shop exercise!
comments.author: @rocketjo

comments.text: I swear i saw you in a JaV
comments.author: @koomloom

comments.text: I guess now you don't even need to know what Canvas and WebGL is to write a web design skill.
comments.author: @훈수빌런-l2x

comments.text: The Sonnet vs Opus split is what stuck with me — Sonnet making small, careful changes while Opus kept adding features until it hit 21,000 lines and started breaking itself. Did you expect the more restrained run to hold up better, or was that a surprise?
comments.author: @TheAIWireShow

comments.text: Try plugging in Google's Elephant and Goldfish method from open sourced GitHub, have 2-3 different A.I. models to be in the conference and decide the flaws of each execution before the build even happens. They will find bugs even before the code is written. Ask Claude to prepare a build pack with their suggestions then use the main builder to build the website. You can actually use Qwen cloud and deposit like $20 and use the Qwen 3.8 flash and Deepseek 4.1 flash to be the bug detector, they cost almost nothing. Claude will set them up and create the Goldfish conference room. I found Deepseek very thorough in bug detection 10X better than Google Argon 4.
comments.author: @mmo3304

comments.text: I personally write an essay for a prompt and put “make it as good as possible” in every line
comments.author: @Destiny0735

comments.text: 4:36 I feel these changes are really not good enough, I would have made an adversarial critique analysis everytime and found creative ideas. Otherwise as you can see it hardly changes much. If AI made it, it needs your input, or another AI’s input, otherwise it just assumes it’s like 80% good.

comments.text: This guy just makes everything look more complicated then it is. Just prompt the dam thing and that's all u need...

comments.text: 100 rounds of 'make it better' with zero direction is basically how most clients give feedback lol. at what round did it stop actually improving and just start piling stuff on?
